title: Evaluating Primary Blast Effects In Vitro
protocol: Obtain an appropriate cell line (e.g., dermal papilla cells).
Culture the cells in a T-75 flask containing minimum essential medium α supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin streptomycin.
Keep the cells at standard culture conditions of 37 °C and 5% CO2 in a humidified environment until they reach 80% confluence.
Aspirate the medium and wash the cells twice in Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Incubate the cells with 2 mL of trypsin/EDTA at standard culture conditions for 5 min.
Check to ensure that cells have successfully dissociated from the flask using a light/phase contrast microscope (with a 10X objective lens).
Add 4 mL of culture medium to neutralize the trypsinization reaction.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 200 x g for 4 min to pellet the cells.
Slowly aspirate the supernatant, taking care not to dislodge the pellet.
Re-suspend the pellet in 5 mL of medium.
Transfer a 20 µL aliquot of the cell suspension to a clean hemocytometer and count the cells using a microscope fitted with a 10X objective lens.
Place three 35 mm dishes inside a 90 mm dish.
Label the 35 mm dishes appropriately.
Add 2 mL of medium to each 35 mm dish.
Seed a total of 5 x 10^4 cells per dish, distributing evenly around each dish.
Incubate experimental samples overnight in standard culture conditions.
Wear steel-toe work boots and a laboratory coat during assembly procedures.
Insert two alignment bars through the bolt holes in the horizontal plane of the outlet flange.
Place a nitrile-rubber gasket sheet over the end of the alignment bars between the outlet flange and the EVOC rig.
Attach the EVOC rig to the outlet flange of the shock tube by sliding it over the alignment bars.
Insert four M24 bolts and washers into the remaining holes.
Position the nuts so that they touch the flange.
Tightly fasten the nuts and bolts sequentially in a diagonally symmetric fashion.
Visually check that the EVOC rig and shock tube have successfully aligned.
Attach a pressure transducer to the EVOC rig.
Connect the pressure transducer to the current source using a sensor cable.
Using a BNC cable, connect the current source to the oscilloscope.
Ensure all release valves and flow controls on the shock tube are closed.
Open the built-in external compressed air line.
Manually turn the pressure regulator clockwise to charge the solenoid to 2.5 bar.
Open the safety valve on the compressed gas bottle by turning it anticlockwise 180°.
Slowly turn the pressure regulator, located on top of the gas bottle, clockwise to increase the pressure to approximately 15 bar.
Prepare the diaphragms by cutting a 0.125 mm-thick plastic sheet into 10 cm x 10 cm squares.
Create handles out of tape and fix them to the top and bottom of the diaphragm.
Position the diaphragm next to the front small flange by the breech chamber carefully using the handles.
Ensure that the diaphragm is straight and correctly positioned before closing the breech.
Secure the diaphragm using four M24 bolts and nuts.
Fasten the nuts and bolts sequentially in a diagonally symmetric fashion tightly.
Perform ultraviolet sterilization to prepare a tissue laminar flow hood.
Clean the hood with a disinfectant solution and 70% ethanol.
Gather all items needed for handling cells prior to/post-shock wave exposure.
Place fresh medium, adhesive gas-permeable membranes, sterile scissors, pipettes, and pipette tips within the sterile hood.
Transfer one 90 mm Petri dish containing three experimental samples from the incubator to the sterile hood.
Cut an adhesive gas-permeable membrane sheet into six squares large enough to cover the top of one 35 mm Petri dish.
Aspirate the medium from the 35 mm Petri dish.
Place the lid to one side and cover with two adhesive gas-permeable membranes sections, ensuring a tight seal between the membrane and the edge of the dish.
Transfer the sample to the EVOC rig and secure it to the base of the fixture so that the top of the dish is aligned with the inner base of the shock tube.
Wear ear defenders when pressurizing the shock tube system.
Wear eye goggles, safety boots, and a laboratory coat when pressurizing the shock tube system.
Turn the flow control knob on the regulator clockwise to allow gas to flow into the flexible hose connecting the compressed air cylinder to the shock tube.
Select either the "Double Breech" inlet for a short-duration shock wave or the "Driver Tube" inlet for an increased wave duration at the bottom of the control panel.
Switch on the DC power source and oscilloscope to acquire the waveform data.
Set the oscilloscope sampling rate to 50.0 MS/s with a record length of 1 M points.
Set a range of 50 mV for firing at 2 bar and 100 mV for above 4 bar.
Turn on the safety lights using the switch on the wall opposite the control panel.
Turn on the switch on the solenoid control box to close the solenoid.
Slowly open the flow control by turning the knob counterclockwise.
Monitor the pressure using the control panel display.
Close the flow control by turning the knob clockwise once the diaphragm burst pressure is reached.
Open the solenoid by turning off the switch on the solenoid control box.
Switch off the safety light using the switch on the wall opposite the control panel.
Transfer the cell sample to the sterile hood.
Remove the adhesive gas-permeable membranes from the dish.
Fill the dish with 2 mL of fresh growth medium.
Assess cell viability following shock wave exposure using a redox indicator assay.
Image live and dead cells using fluorescent imaging.
Transfer 200 μL of the redox indicator reagent to each experimental dish directly after refilling them with 2 mL of medium post-shock wave exposure.
Incubate at standard culture conditions for 4 h.
Transfer 2 x 100 µL aliquots of the mixture in a dark sterile hood to either a black or clear 96-well plate, depending on whether fluorescence or absorbance will be used to assess viability.

Transfer the 96-well plate to an appropriate plate reader fitted with the correct filters and read using excitation bands 530ex/590em for fluorescence or 70 nm combined with a 600-nm reference for absorbance.
Export and save the data.
Analyze the data to identify any difference between shock wave-exposed samples and non-exposed controls, as this can indicate a drop in cell viability.
Aspirate the medium containing the redox indicator reagent.
Replace it with 2 mL of fresh medium and incubate the cells at standard culture conditions for 24 h.
Repeat the above steps as necessary to obtain a second viability time point.
For the fluorescent imaging of live and dead cells, aspirate the medium.
Wash the cells twice in 1 mL of PBS.
Transfer 100 µL of the complete reagent found in the imaging kit to each sample.
Incubate at room temperature protected from light for 15 min.
Aspirate the reagent.
Wash once using 1 mL of PBS.
Carefully remove the coverslip from the 35 mm dish using fine point forceps.
Place the coverslip face-down onto a glass microscopy slide.
Acquire images for each sample using a fluorescent microscope with a 10X objective lens and 0.50 numerical aperture.
Fit the correct excitation and emission filters (ex/em 488 nm/515 nm and 570 nm/602 nm).
Count the number of live cells from each image using image analysis software.
Count the number of dead or dying cells with red fluorescence from each image using image analysis software.
